idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to a user's interaction history. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items by dot product. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
idea.motivation: Attention can select relevant recent actions while retaining access to longer histories, adapting to differing interaction densities. The supplied 'cold start' title describes a starting baseline; SASRec itself does not solve recommendation for completely unseen items or users without history. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781)
idea.implementation_notes: Use RecHarness sasrec_perdataset with all four category routes. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment default of 200 epochs. Select configurations using only the pinned macro validation HR@10. Keep artifacts within the trial directory and execution on one GPU. Architecture changes must update both the predictor writer and DiagnosisProbe compatibility. No benchmark results or improvements have been established here.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged training split.
  Build padded histories, shifted positive targets, and sampled negatives.
  Encode histories with item/position embeddings and causal attention blocks.
  Minimize sampled binary cross-entropy on non-padding targets.
  Save model configuration and weights beneath the trial directory.
Write a predictor that restores the matching architecture and routes each category.
Use the host's macro validation HR@10 to compare trials.

originality.positive: Provides a well-defined sequential recommendation baseline.
originality.negative: Applying the published SASRec architecture to the matched task introduces little methodological novelty.

future_potential.positive: Sequence length, regularization, sampling, and loss choices provide concrete directions for validation-based search.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured; sparse histories and unseen item embeddings limit the baseline.

code_difficulty.positive: The supplied SASRec compatibility contract closely matches the baseline architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Training, saved architecture, category routing, predictor generation, and diagnostic probes must remain consistent.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
